https://x.com/cosmosarcive/status/210740.text:
A gravitational wave does not push space like a wave pushes water. It changes the geometry of spacetime itself.

When two massive objects spiral together, their accelerating motion creates ripples that travel outward at the speed of light. As a wave passes, distances stretch in one direction while contracting in the perpendicular direction. This alternating distortion is why gravitational waves have a distinctive quadrupole pattern.

The remarkable part is how tiny the effect is. LIGO’s first detection in 2015 measured a strain of roughly 10⁻²¹, meaning a 4 km arm changed length by far less than the width of a proton.

We are not simply detecting waves. We are measuring spacetime moving.
